cultural.vision_reason: This is an indigo tie-resist dyed boubou/tobe gown made from a rectangular cloth with a head-hole, a garment type well documented among Wolof and neighboring Senegambian peoples using indigo resist-dye techniques on European calico.

physical.title: gown; textile
physical.summary: Gown (boubou, tobe); composed of a single width of European calico cotton, forming a rectangle. A circular hole has been cut into the centre for the wearer’s head. The cloth has been tie resist-dyed indigo along the weft in such a way to produce four wide bands of striations between five narrower bands of solid indigo. The entire cloth was twice dyed in indigo, once overall, and again after the ties had been removed to form a lighter blue decoration within the four decorative bands.

cultural.vision_reason: Close-up of an indigo-dyed, wax-resist combed cotton cloth, consistent with a Wolof indigo boubou/tobe gown textile as described; wax-resist indigo textiles of this type are made and worn in Senegal/Wolof context.

physical.title: gown; textile
physical.summary: Indigo gown (boubou, tobe), composed of a single width of European calico cotton, forming a rectangle. A slit has been cut into the centre for the wearer’s head. With the exception of the area surrounded the slit and the two ends, the cloth has been covered with wax into which streaks have been drawn with a comb. After dying in an indigo bath, this produces a combed area of white and light blue against ends and neck area of dark blue.

physical.title: gown; textile
physical.summary: Gown (boubou, tobe); composed of two widths of imported European calico cloth machine-sewn together to form a rectangle. A circular hole has been cut into the centre for the wearer’s head. Gown has four horizontal bands of indigo stitch resist-dyed patterns. The entire cloth has been twice dyed in indigo, once overall, and again after the ties were removed to form a lighter blue decoration within the four decorative bands.
